claim_boundary: V10 has no aggregate result and cannot be described as PASS, FAIL, or INCONCLUSIVE aggregate evidence. It consumed one attempt: claude-v8-remediation-confirmation-v10-r1 is a single valid FAIL observation (overall_score 88.67 below the 90 floor, C0/H0/M8, V8-T4 reopened mechanically) when replayed with the one corrected integrity key, and the frozen v10 validator still rejects it. Under v10's FAIL-first rule no completed v10 aggregate could have passed. The successor carries r1 as its first scheduled attempt and cannot overturn, replace, or erase it, so any completed successor aggregate is FAIL. The reviewed object is source snapshot d01dc69d, not any shipped release. V10 was committed frozen twice before r1 (474b3d1, then re-frozen in place at 679f2c4 on a different packet under the same schedule digest), and r1 is the only attempt reserved under either freeze. The canonical v10 archive stays FROZEN with no attempts, and r1's bytes exist only outside it. This record does not change v8 or the v9 record, and it is not evidence about the product beyond that single observation.

freeze_history.disclosure: V10 was committed frozen twice before any reservation. The first committed freeze, in release commit 474b3d1, shipped as v10 frozen in the 1.11.0 release commit and in tags v1.12.0 through v1.15.1. Commit 679f2c4 deleted that packet and re-froze v10 in place under the same protocol ID, schedule digest 6288fea9, attempt IDs, remediation ledger, and model catalog: the protocol changed only in its packet.freeze_policy text, all seven reviewed source files changed, and the packet, manifest, source snapshot, prompt-size attestation, v10 runner, evidence validator, and shared zero-tool runner digests changed. The 679f2c4 commit message and CHANGELOG changes do not mention v10, and its benchmarks/STATUS.md changes state only that v10 is frozen and not run. CHANGELOG [1.11.0] separately records an earlier, never separately committed v10 packet whose 877,407-byte prompt claude-opus-5 rejected for length and which was reduced before 474b3d1. r1 is the only attempt ever reserved under any v10 freeze, and it ran under the 679f2c4 freeze.

measured_state.note: Measured at the v10 freeze and replayed exactly before r1, when prepare-only output matched the frozen packet, manifest, and prompt-size attestation. The token count is a pinned o200k_base size proxy, not Anthropic tokenization and not a context-window fit.

reason: V10 froze at 679f2c4, reserved its first scheduled attempt, called claude-opus-5 once, and wrote a decisive report. Every later attempt is then blocked before reservation: the frozen runner writes superseded_phase_record_sha256 into integrity_before and integrity_after, while the frozen evidence validator builds its expected integrity without that key and compares the whole dictionary, so it rejects the r1 report, and the runner validates the archive before every reservation. Repairing either file changes a digest bound by the v10 freeze, and amending a frozen protocol after observing a result would destroy the value of preregistering it. That 679f2c4 freeze was itself a second committed freeze: v10 had already been frozen and shipped at 474b3d1 and was replaced in place before any reservation, with a different packet under the same schedule digest, and that replacement was not disclosed at the time (execution_provenance.freeze_history). V10 is therefore recorded as superseded after a measured infrastructure finding rather than amended again. The cause is harness-only: the unit suite never passed a runner-written live report through the integrity comparison. It is not a model, prompt, or product finding.
